description: Returns every NCR linked to any input on this traveler, as a flat array the client filters by input name — same shape convention as the existing GET /travelers/:id/notes/ endpoint. New endpoint; no existing route changes.
authorization: Same as viewing the traveler itself — reqUtils.canReadMw('id') (the traveler's own existing read-access gate). No additional NCR-specific access check, per spec.md's resolved clarification that traveler access alone governs visibility of a linked NCR's link/status.

id.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the Traveler document

body.input_name: string — matches a TravelerData.name / form.labels key on this traveler
body.status: string — one of the existing NCR_STATUSES

not_found_404.body: Traveler not found (reqUtils.exist('id', Traveler)'s existing behavior)

forbidden_403.body: Not authorized to read this traveler (reqUtils.canReadMw('id')'s existing behavior)

notes: Query: Ncr.find({'traveler_link.traveler_id': id, 'traveler_link.initiated_from_traveler': true}, {ncr_number:1, status:1, 'traveler_link.input_name':1}).lean(), reshaped to the flat array above
An input with zero linked NCRs simply has no entries in the array — the client shows only the 'Initiate NCR' action (if touched) and no badges

Multiple entries can share the same input_name (spec.md FR-008 — an input can accumulate more than one linked NCR over time); the client groups/filters by input_name client-side, exactly as the existing notes endpoint's array is filtered by name
Entries are sorted newest first (Ncr.created_at descending, _id descending as the tie-break); the client keeps that order and shows each NCR of an input in its own row, so the latest is on top
